The Indianapolis Colts are 2-6 on the season after their 42-7 defeat at the hands of the Jacksonville Jaguars that led to a Josh Downs no-show in the locker room . Colts RB Jonathan Taylor had a rough day at the office then sent a stern message after the game, on a day when Anthony Richardson replaced Daniel Jones at QB. Calls amplified for Richardson to be the starter going forward after the game, with the Colts pondering a potential fire sale at the upcoming NFL Trade Deadline. Richardson’s career could still take off, but if it’s going to happen, he will need to continue to do exactly what he said and make sure he’s ready when the time comes, because opportunities to start at QB in the National Football League don’t come often. item.title: Orlando Magic coach Sean Swinney on how Boston Celtics beat his team defensively
item.description: The Boston Celtics defended aggressively and on a string in their 108-97 road won against the Orlando Magic , and Magic head coach Sean Sweeney let it be known that the sting of the Celtics defense stood out to him as a major contributing factor to Orlando losing the contest while speaking to the media postgame. "I thought down the stretch, there were a few times that we attacked and did a good job of getting to the paint and then didn't quite have a couple of outcomes that we would have liked to have seen," said Sweeney. "And then defensively, they had a couple tough shots made by (Jayson) Tatum." "Obviously, he had a very nice game," said the Orlando coach. "Got to the line 17 times, fouled them twice or three times on jump shots, and then a couple offensive rebound 3s for them down the stretch ... We were right there. We just needed a couple more plays to go our way." "It's definitely a combination of things," continued Sweeney. "I think when you see that crowd, being able to make that right play to your teammate, is really important." "And credit them, they force turnovers," he added. "They're aggressive to go for steals. There's a number of times where you have to be really strong with the ball and then play through contact when you do get it." "And we can do a better job of that. Love the aggressiveness, but both halves, I thought we could have been better with the basketball there and taken care of it." item.title: N.Y. Mets pitching great, '69 Series hero Jerry Koosman dies at 86
item.description: Jerry Koosman, praised as the best left-handed pitcher in New York Mets history and a key figure in the team's iconic 1969 World Series victory, has died at age 86, the team announced Sunday. File Photo by John Angelillo/UPI Nov. 1 (UPI) -- Jerry Koosman, one of the greatest pitchers in the history of the New York Mets and a hero of their iconic 1969 World Series victory, has died at age 83, the team announced Sunday. Considered the best left-handed pitcher in Mets history, he is most fondly remembered as the winner of Game 2 of the historic series against Baltimore during which he held the Orioles hitless through six innings en route to a 2-1 win. The victory evened the series at one victory apiece and helped set the stage for the "Amazin' Mets" to pull off what was then the most improbable world championship in baseball history. We are saddened to share the news that Jerry Koosman has passed away. We send our thoughts and prayers to his family. https://t.co/8zriJmxCBe— New York Mets (@Mets) November 1, 2026 "Kooz was one of the greatest pitchers in team history and a beloved member of the Mets family," team owners Steve and Alex Cohen said in a statement. "The 1969 Miracle Mets were filled with heroes, and the special southpaw from Appleton, Minnesota, was central to their success. "He was a fierce competitor on the field, and respected teammate in the clubhouse. His legendary performance in the World Series helped the Mets secure their first Championship in team history. "On behalf of the entire Mets organization, we extend our heartfelt condolences to Jerry's family, friends, former teammates and all who loved him." Koosman pitched 12 years of his 19-season career with New York from 1967-78, winning 140 games and posting a 3.09 ERA. He recorded a 21-win season in 1976 and still holds many team records for left-handed pitchers, including starts (346), complete games (108), shutouts (26, tied with Jon Matlack), wins (140), decisions (277), innings (2,544 2/3) and strikeouts (1,799), according to MLB.com . He teamed up with Tom Seaver starting in 1968 to give the Mets a powerful 1-2 punch atop their rotation -- a tandem which lasted until Seaver was traded to the Cincinnati Reds in June 1977. Koosman (No. 36), Seaver (No. 41) and catcher Mike Piazza (No. 31) are the only three Mets players to have their numbers retired from the team.

item.title: Chicago Cubs news: Pete Crow-Armstrong, Alex Bregman win Gold Gloves
item.description: MIAMI, FL - SEPTEMBER 04: Pete Crow-Armstrong #4 of the Chicago Cubs makes a leaping catch for the out in the sixth inning during the game between the Chicago Cubs and the Miami Marlins at loanDepot park on Friday, September 4, 2026 in Miami, Florida. (Photo by Kelly Gavin/MLB Photos via Getty Images) | MLB Photos via Getty Images The Rawlings Gold Glove Awards were announced tonight and two Cubs players, center fielder Pete Crow-Armstrong and third baseman Alex Bregman, came home with the trophies. It was the second-straight win in center field for Crow-Armstrong. It also Bregman’s second Gold Glove, having previously won the award with the Astros in 2024. Bregman also became the first Cubs third baseman to win a Gold Glove since Ron Santo in 1968. Josiah Hartshorn, the Cubs’ top prospect, also won a minor league Gold Glove as the top defensive first baseman across all of the minor leagues. Crow-Armstrong beat the Dodgers’ Andy Pages and the Braves’ Michael Harris for the award in center field. Bregman topped the Dodgers’ Max Muncy and the Marlins’ Javier Sanoja for the honors at third base. Three other Cubs were finalists for a Gold Glove, but came up short. Ian Happ, who has won the Gold Glove in each of the past four seasons, lost this time to the Brewers Jackson Chourio. Right fielder Seiya Suzuki was among the top three in right field, but the award went to the Diamondbacks’ Corbin Carroll. Shortstop Dansby Swanson, who won the award twice with Atlanta, lost out to the D-Backs’ Geraldo Perdomo. There is still the Platinum Glove Award to be given out, and you can vote for Crow-Armstrong or Bregman at Rawlings dot com.

item.title: Cole Young wins first-ever Gold Glove at second base
item.description: May 26, 2026; West Sacramento, California, USA; Seattle Mariners second baseman Cole Young (2) fields a line drive against against the Athletics during the seventh inning at Sutter Health Park. Mandatory Credit: Dennis Lee-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Tonight was the announcement of the 2026 Rawlings Gold Glove Awards. The Mariners, being one of the league’s worst-fielding teams, unsurprisingly had but one nomination: Cole Young at second base. That one nomination really counted, though, as Cole Young won, giving the Mariners their 45th Gold Glove award as a team, the first since 2024 (when they had two winners in Julio Rodríguez and Cal Raleigh), and the first at second base for the Mariners since 2004, the last year of Brett Boone’s historic three-peat at the position (when Cole Young was one year old). Perhaps speaking to how haunted the second base position has been for the Mariners over the years, Young is just the third Mariner to win a Gold Glove at the position. He is also the second Mariners player to win a Gold Glove Award in his age-22 season or younger, joining Ken Griffey Jr. – not bad company to be in. View Link Young edged out White Sox second baseman Chase Meidroth and Royals second baseman Michael Massey to win the award. Both Meidroth and Massey had the edge via Outs Above Average (OAA), MLB’s in-house stat, and Meidroth led all AL second baseman with +10 Defensive Run Value (DRV). The official MLB writeup of the nominations listed Young as a distant third behind those two, tepidly noting “different metrics had considerably different opinions of Young’s defense in 2026.” Where Young did shine was in Defensive Runs Saved (DRS), a stat tracked by Sports Info Solutions; Young led all AL second basemen with 16 DRS – that’s the most by a Mariners second baseman in a season since SIS began tracking the statistic in 2003. Young’s .990 fielding percentage is the third-best single-season mark by a second baseman in Mariners history, trailing only Robinson Canó (.996 in 2016 and .991 in 2015). View Link Of course, anyone reading this has seen Young’s play for themselves, which speaks louder than any defensive metrics, which count for just 25% of the vote total – the rest of the vote comes from managers and coaches from each league. We’ve been writing about Young’s improved defense at second base since spring training , when it became immediately obvious that Young had improved on both sides of the ball. Young improved his footwork and positioning significantly, finally settling in at second base after working at shortstop for most of his playing career. While the arm action is unconventional, I encourage anyone evaluating Cole Young to look at his footwork first; range metrics don’t like him (hence the bad OAA mark), but he’s incredibly quick and light on his feet, almost dancer-like, something he drills every day with over-exaggerated hops during his infield work. item.title: Ducks Notebook: Terry, Moore return to practice, Jensen clears waivers, Klepov to juniors
item.description: Anaheim Ducks right wing Troy Terry (19) during an NHL hockey game against the Nashville Predators, Tuesday April 7, 2026 in Anaheim, Calif. IRVINE, Calif. – Saturday was a busy small news day around the Anaheim Ducks. Aside from the eyebrow-raising selection of Laurent Brossoit as the starting goaltender for the Ducks tonight against the Ottawa Senators ahead of a healthy Lukáš Dostál and Ville Husso, Saturday’s practice at Great Park ice saw a handful of returns to the ice for Pavel Mintyukov, Troy Terry and Ian Moore and the departures, for now, of Nick Jensen and Nikita Klepov. Here’s a run through the the practice notebook detailing the Ducks’ personnel moves: Pavel Mintyukov Elevated Off Injured Reserve First and most pertinent, Pavel Mintyukov was in the regular line rushes on Saturday and was brought off injured reserve from his lower-body injury. Mintyukov was Oct. 20 on Long Island and has missed the last four games. He will be paired with Noah Warren on the blue line against Ottawa on Sunday. The 22-year-old Russian has averaged over 18 minutes per game and is third among Ducks defensemen in expected goal share at five-on-five, with Anaheim earning 51.15% xGF with Mintyukov on the ice. Troy Terry, Ian Moore Return to Practice After Season-Long Absence Second, and maybe the biggest needed morale boost the Ducks could use right now, was the return of their longest-tenured player in Troy Terry and much needed help on the blue line in Ian Moore. Terry underwent hip surgery in June for a chronic hip impingement and labral tear and initially had a recovery timeline stretching into late November or early December. Now, Terry skated in his first full practice with the team and is just a week or so away from his season debut, according to Joel Quenneville. Terry remains on long-term injured reserve, which provides the Ducks nearly $4 million in salary cap relief. “It was just fun to be back with the guys and feel like part of the team again,” Terry said, “and try to take the puck from me. I’ve been skating by myself for a long time… Still working towards it.” Terry has been around the Ducks facility since the beginning of training camp and could often be seen catching bits of practice from the other side of the glass. After battling through his injury as long as he did last season, he’s excited to be back with the group. “It’s hard. It’s hard to not start the year too,” Terry said. “You just feel very much removed. It’s hard to not be around the guys… Just trying to support where I can. item.title: Brewers nab two Gold Glove Awards
item.description: MILWAUKEE, WI - OCTOBER 24: Brice Turang #2 and Jackson Chourio #11 of the Milwaukee Brewers celebrate after defeating the Tampa Bay Rays in Game Two of the 2026 World Series presented by Capital One at American Family Field on Saturday, October 24, 2026 in Milwaukee, Wisconsin. (Photo by Mary DeCicco/MLB Photos via Getty Images) | MLB Photos via Getty Images This evening, the Rawlings Gold Glove Award winners were announced for the 70th time in Major League Baseball history. After missing out on any Gold Glove Award winners a year ago, the Brewers entered tonight with two nominees: second baseman Brice Turang and left fielder Jackson Chourio. It’s quite fitting that the man who fielded the final out of the Brewers’ first-ever World Series Championship also earned his second career Gold Glove. As spectacular as Turang was in the postseason, not allowing anything by him, it’s important to note that those plays aren’t factored into the voting. Turang, who won a Gold Glove and Platinum Glove in 2024, led MLB second basemen with 23 defensive runs saved this season, playing a large role in his award. Champion. 2x Gold Glover. Best 2B in baseball. 🏆🏆 Congrats, Brice! pic.twitter.com/wgWh0qwnj6 — Milwaukee Brewers (@Brewers) November 2, 2026 Turang beat out a pair of his National League Central rivals in JJ Wetherholt of the St. Louis Cardinals and Brandon Lowe of the Pittsburgh Pirates. Wetherholt, who was a rookie in 2026, led MLB in fielding run value while subsequently leading the Outs Above Average (OAA) category by six over Turang. Lowe was slightly below both Turang and Wetherholt in many of the same categories. For the first time in franchise history, the Brewers will have a left field Gold Glove winner, as Chourio locked in his first of his career. Chourio’s NL-leading Fielding Run Value helped him beat out Daylen Lile of the Washington Nationals and Ian Happ of the Cubs. Lile was fourth among left fielders with eight Defensive Runs Saved in just his second season in the big leagues, while Happ led all of the NL with nine outfield assists. A Gold Glover and World Series Champion at age 22❕ Congrats, Jackson! pic.twitter.com/JMeX6c6h2K — Milwaukee Brewers (@Brewers) November 2, 2026 Over the first few seasons of his career, Chourio bounced around every position in the outfield. First, before Brewers management decided to keep Christian Yelich as the full-time designated hitter, Chourio found himself splitting time between right field and center field. This past season, the Brewers had Garrett Mitchell for a full 162-game season, allowing Chourio to settle into his role in left field, playing 123 of his 137 games there. This is just the third time in franchise history that the Brewers have had two players win the Gold Glove in the same year, and the first time since 2024 that Turang and Sal Frelick both won. He asserted himself well in that game, finishing with 32 points, four rebounds, and seven assists on 8-of-19 shooting from the field, and he added two blocks for good measure. item.title: Florida State Bringing Back Jimbo Fisher as Head Coach Would Have Major Financial Incentive
item.description: Jimbo Fisher leaving Florida State created a domino effect throughout the country. Getty Florida State needs a new head football coach after parting ways with Mike Norvell on Sunday. Could they go back to an old friend, Jimbo Fisher? That’s definitely something that will be floated as an idea, no matter how realistic it is or isn’t. There would be at least one obvious reason to bring Fisher back, and it has to do with money — which is ironic, considering that Fisher got a massive buyout when he left Texas A&M in 2023 and hasn’t coached since then. Why Florida State Would Re-Hire Jimbo Fisher Fisher’s massive buyout from Texas A&M would save the Seminoles money. The Athletic’s Chris Vannini summed it up in an article on Sunday with this paragraph: “We might as well start here. One segment of the FSU faithful wants Fisher back. He led Florida State to that 2013 national title, but he got the largest buyout in college football history ($77.6 million) from Texas A&M upon his firing in 2023, and he hasn’t coached since then. Rerun hires almost never work out well, but Fisher would help solve the money problem because he is able to take a lower salary with that Texas A&M money still coming his way, and no buyout will be required to hire him away from someone else. Don’t worry about the fact that he left Tallahassee for College Station amid a 5-6 season, apparently, because some people still remember the good days.” This would be a bit, in a weird way, like the Minnesota Vikings signing Kyler Murray and the Atlanta Falcons signing Tua Tagovailoa as free agents in the past NFL offseason. They both had huge cap hits with their former teams and got cheap contracts to play quarterback with their new teams. Fisher would work similarly for Florida State. Jimbo Fisher Record at Florida State Fisher coached at Florida State from 2010 through 2017. In that time, he had an 83-23 record. That included a 14-0 season in 2013 when they won the national championship with Jameis Winston at quarterback. Fisher also had FSU go 12-2 in 2012 and 13-1 in 2014. In addition to the BCS National Championship, FSU won the Chick-fil-A Bowl, the Champs Sports Bowl, the Orange Bowl and the Orange Bowl again while Fisher was at Florida State. They spent most of Fisher’s tenure ranked in the AP Top-25. Fisher ended with a 5-6 mark in his last season, and that’s when he left for Texas A&M. It would certainly be a headline-grabbing move for the Seminoles to bring back Fisher. It might also be a fun move toward recruiting wins. It’s something to keep an eye on. item.title: Todd Monken Defends Jared Verse After Browns Lopsided Loss to Steelers
item.description: Browns head coach defends Jared Verse. Getty Jared Verse called out the Steelers and failed to defend his words. Getty The Cleveland Browns suffered a lopsided loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers on the road on Sunday. Cleveland entered the game tied with the Steelers for the best record in the AFC North. With the loss, the Browns fell to 5-3 and will now go on the road to play the New Orleans Saints. Cleveland Browns HC Defends Jared Verse Getty Jared Verse called out the Steelers and failed to defend his words. Before the game, Browns pass rusher Jared Verse said the Steelers don’t worry him, and no one on the team does. It gave Pittsburgh some bulletin board material, but after the game, Monken claimed Verse’s words had no impact on the result. “Ultimately, whether it’s me or our team, it’s not what you say, it’s what you do and how you play. And that’s in life, that’s not a Jared Verse thing. It’s what we do, not what we say. And we did not do the things today that give you a chance to win and when that happens, the scoreboard’s gonna look like that. And then you gotta eat it,” Monken said postgame . It’s not a surprise to see Monken have his players back, but Verse also had another lackluster game. He was a key part of the trade return for Myles Garrett, and he’s yet to make an impact for the Browns. Against the Steelers, Verse had just 1 tackle . He’s yet to record a sack this season with the Browns, which is a major problem. item.description: Jordan Godfree-Imagn Images Atlanta United cannot reach the 2026 Audi MLS Cup Playoffs, yet head coach Tata Martino insists Sunday’s match against Toronto FC holds more weight than a typical end-of-season game. The surprising reality is that this final home fixture is not about the current standings but about shaping the team’s future. Martino stated that the upcoming game is vital because “it sets the tone for how we will start next season.” This means the players on the field today are playing for the 2027 campaign, not just the remaining minutes of 2026. The 5-Stripes have not won a home match in their last six tries, a streak that hurts pride in the city. However, the team aims to end this slide against Toronto FC, who currently sit in 11th place in the league table. Atlanta already swept their Canadian rivals this year, having beaten CF Montréal in October and Toronto FC back in April. Those earlier wins came from a free kick by Alexey Miranchuk and a special strike by Tristan Muyumba. The squad now wants to replicate that success to give the fans a reason to celebrate before the year ends. Building Trust When the Scoreboard Fails Player Tristan Muyumba believes the team can still find success despite the tough season. He spoke on Friday about the group’s mindset, noting that “I believe a lot because I trust in my teammates and I know everyone wants to do the good thing.” This trust is crucial because the team has struggled to keep up their effort for full ninety-minute games. The second half of their recent match in New York showed how hard it is to maintain that level, and how small moments can change the result. Muyumba argues that good play matters even when the final score does not go their way. He explained that “It’s important because those kind of performances, even when the result is not the one we expect, help for confidence.” The goal is to keep the good habits from games like the Chicago effort where the team moved the ball with fluidity. They need to fix the bad habits to be ready for the last two games of the schedule. This focus on quality over results is a strange but necessary approach for a team out of playoff contention. Fans Who Stayed Through the Hard Times The fans in Atlanta have shown up through the difficult days and the good ones. During challenging moments of the season, they consistently stood by us. The team knows the trial extends from the field to the city streets, and the players want to repay that support. They are fighting to make the fans proud on Sunday. Per Atlanta United FC , the team plans to use these final matches to root out bad habits while building on the good ones. The visitors from Toronto have conceded more goals this year than the hosts, which makes the attacking phase critical for Atlanta. Winning at home is the only way to turn the tide on the last six-match losing streak. The squad wants to give the fans a win and a good performance before the season closes.

item.title: Matt Olson, Mauricio Dubon win Gold Gloves for Atlanta Braves
item.description: HOUSTON, TEXAS - SEPTEMBER 20: Matt Olson #28 and Mauricio Dubon #14 of the Atlanta Braves celebrate winning the National League East title after a game against the Houston Astros at Daikin Park on September 20, 2026 in Houston, Texas. (Photo by Joe Buvid/Getty Images) | Getty Images Matt Olson and Mauricio Dubon both won Gold Gloves on Sunday night, a deserved recognition for two of the most reliable defenders in the National League. It was the fourth time Olson has won a Gold Glove in his career. Olson took home the Gold Glove hardware in 2025 with Atlanta, plus won two additional times in the American League with the Oakland Athletics in 2018 and 2019. It was a no-brainer to award Olson the Gold Glove, who has established himself as the best in the game at his position the last few years. Olson led all first basemen in Outs Above Average (+12) this past season, and he was +11 Defensive Runs Saved on the corner. Olson is also a strong receiver of the baseball and does a strong job picking any errant throws from his infield peers. As for Dubon, it’s the third time he’s won a Gold Glove. He took home the hardware as a utility man with the Houston Astros in 2023 and 2025. Dubon was stellar defensively in his first season with the Braves, playing all over the diamond. He ranked in the 91st percentile in Outs Above Average and graded out well with his throwing ability as well. Dubon’s ability to play any position on the field is pretty incredible to watch on a nightly basis. The Braves had two Gold Glove nominees in addition to Olson and Dubon: starter Chris Sale and center fielder Michael Harris. The National League gold glove for pitchers went to Nolan McLean of the Mets. Harris, while certainly deserving of a Gold Glove, fell short to Pete Crow Armstrong of the Cubs.

item.title: Nolan McLean wins Gold Glove
item.description: NEW YORK, NEW YORK - MAY 31: Nolan McLean #26 of the New York Mets in action against the Miami Marlins at Citi Field on May 31, 2026 in New York City. The Mets defeated the Marlins 10-1. (Photo by Jim McIsaac/Getty Images) | Getty Images The 2026 Rawlings Gold Glove Award winners were announced tonight on ESPN, and the Mets had three finalists in the running for the National League awards: Carson Benge at right field, Luis Torrens at catcher, and Nolan McLean at starting pitcher. Luis Torrens: This was Torrens’ second year in a row as a Gold Glove finalist. Ostensibly a backup catcher, he was behind the dish in 86 games for 673.2 innings. His Defensive Runs Saved (DRS) was +12, his Fielding Run Value (FRV) was +10, and his pop time was 1.86 seconds. His fWAR was 2.1. Not all of his competition this evening played full-time either. He faced Freddy Fermin, who played 660.2 innings as catcher for the Padres, and Gabriel Moreno of the Diamondbacks, who played a more regular 886.0 innings as their first-string backstop. Ultimately, Moreno, who also ranked second in DRS among catchers, took home the Gold Glove. Nolan McLean (winner): In 31 games (179.2 innings), McLean tallied +4 DRS (fifth among major-league pitchers), 16 putouts, and 24 assists. Runners only attempted to steal eight times when he was on the mound in all of 2026. He had an impressive rookie campaign, with an fWAR of 3.5, and is also a contender for Rookie of the Year. McLean won against Michael McGreevey of the Cardinals and Chris Sale of the Braves. He is the first rookie pitcher to win a Gold Glove. Ron Darling is the only other Mets pitcher to win, when he did so in 1989. Carson Benge: Deemed to have the most valuable arm in baseball (as measured by Statcast’s aptly-named metric, Arm Value), Benge had 259 putouts and 10 assists from the outfield in 2026. He played in right field for 134 games and 1140.0 innings. During that time, his DRS and FRV were both +6. Overall, his fWAR was 4.3. His defense is one reason that he is a contender for Rookie of the Year alongside McLean. Benge faced Seiya Suzuki of the Cubs, who had the second-highest DRS among right fielders, and the winner, Corbin Carroll of the Diamondbacks, who was in the 95th percentile among right fielders in outs above average (10). Platinum Glove voting begins on Rawlings.com and goes through November 5 at 11:59 PM ET. The winner will be determined by the fan vote and the SABR Defensive Index (SDI) and announced on November 6 during the Rawlings Gold Glove Award Ceremony.

item.description: Lewis Hamilton had to settle for third after securing his first pole position with Ferrari in Mexico [Getty Images] Lewis Hamilton says Ferrari "have to have some serious talks behind closed doors" after fighting between their two drivers cost them victory in the Mexico City Grand Prix. Leclerc cut a chicane on the first lap to take the lead from Hamilton, who then lost second place to Max Verstappen as a consequence of his team-mate's attack. Verstappen went on to win the race with Hamilton second, as Kimi Antonelli finished third to become the youngest world champion in Formula 1 history. "Ultimately, that lost us the win today," said Hamilton. "We have to have some serious talks behind closed doors." During a red-flag period in the race caused by a crash for Valtteri Bottas' Cadillac, Hamilton had said over team radio: "We've got big problems. Big, big problems." When informed Hamilton was unhappy, Leclerc said: "I will speak with Lewis. We both didn't make the corner. I don't know if Lewis' point was for me to get P3 but having the Red Bull second I felt it was worth it to keep the position and see what happened. That's what I did. "I could be also unhappy with how much he pushed me off track out of Turn One, but it is racing. When you are fighting for a win it is the way it should be." Hamilton's point is that if the Ferraris had worked together on the first lap, they would have been running one-two and could have controlled the race from there and likely finished in those positions. He said: "We could have easily had a one-two today. We had the pace to do so. "We're going into Turn Four first and second. If we just held position, I think anything can happen in the race.
